title: Post-call qualification — illustrative recommendations
headline: After a customer call, preparing qualification updates may be worth investigating.
provenance_note: Synthetic example — not a production finding

objective.description: Explore whether post-call preparation could become easier while salespeople retain account judgment.
objective.north_star: Useful, source-supported qualification updates with less total preparation and review effort; baseline and target not established.

attributes.label: Technology landscape
attributes.value: Illustrative constraint: Claude Code may be used with redacted files; Salesforce remains the system of record. Salesforce API access is neither tested nor granted; existing meeting-assistant features are unevaluated.

attributes.label: Acceptable assistance
attributes.value: Explore a prompt, an assistant, or an existing feature. Do not assume an autonomous workflow is required.

attributes.label: Boundaries
attributes.value: Salespeople own final account judgment and CRM changes. Do not upload customer information without the organization’s permission; use representative redacted examples for this illustration.

current_state.description: In this synthetic situation, a salesperson finishes a customer call, reopens the transcript and updates qualification fields. A manager later reviews those fields for deal preparation. The connection between those activities is a hypothesis until a linked example is supplied.
current_state.snapshot: Synthetic demonstration created 2026-10-06; no Work Brain production evidence was fetched for this example.
details: The salesperson reads the transcript and recalls account context.
The salesperson decides which MEDDPICC fields have new supported information.
The manager may use those fields for deal review; no observed handoff is claimed.
current_state.coverage: Two illustrative notes describe the work. They are not measured observations, executions, exception rates or organizational cadence.

process_index.title: Update qualification after a customer call
Prepare for a manager deal review

relations.rationale: A linked deal example could establish whether the same field updates are used in manager review; this is not an observed handoff.

recommendations.description: Identify a plausible place to reduce repetitive preparation, then use concrete artifacts and user corrections to decide which assistance would help.
assumptions: The described work exists as repeated work in the intended team; this example does not establish that fact.
ignore_if: The salesperson’s main difficulty is deciding deal strategy rather than preparing evidence.

problems.title: After a customer call, the salesperson re-reads the transcript to update qualification fields
problems.recover: Potentially less repetitive preparation; value unmeasured
problems.statement: A salesperson has to decide what the call changes about qualification, then fill in MEDDPICC fields. Re-reading and evidence transfer may be repetitive, but account judgment remains human.
problems.recover_detail: Understand the time spent preparing evidence and correcting drafts before estimating any saving.
problems.owner: Salesperson; sales manager confirms the quality standard
problems.source_summary: SYN-1 and SYN-2 — synthetic notes only
problems.note: This is a work hypothesis, not an instruction to build an agent.
details: Review the call transcript and any earlier account context.
Map supported evidence to the field definitions.
Leave unsupported fields unknown, record the update, and review with a manager when needed.

counts.limitations: Synthetic notes are not independent executions. Counts must not be used as a repetition or impact proxy.

solutions.name: Explore a source-linked qualification draft
solutions.what: A reviewable assistant could turn one customer-call transcript into cited MEDDPICC field suggestions for the salesperson; the form remains provisional.
solutions.future: After a call, the salesperson provides a transcript and the field rubric. The assistant proposes field updates with quotes and unknowns. The salesperson checks each suggestion before changing the CRM.
solutions.impact_reasoning: Potential value is less re-reading and transcription. Net time and correction cost are unknown until we see linked examples and the current workflow. This is not measured ROI.
solutions.people_keep: Salesperson validates and updates the CRM
solutions.selection_summary: Variable language may map to a stable rubric, and individual suggestions could be checked against quotes. A transcript search and checklist may already be enough.
assumptions: Salespeople repeatedly translate transcripts into the same qualification fields.
solutions.counter_hypothesis: The fields may depend on relationship judgment accumulated across many conversations, rather than information present in one transcript.
ignore_if: An existing tool already produces trusted field suggestions with less review effort.
challenges: Unsupported inferences about budget or authority could create misleading deal records.
form_factors: A manually invoked prompt with the rubric and a transcript
An assistant that drafts a review table
Extend an existing CRM feature if it provides the same useful result
selection_details: Model fit: synthesis with a stable output schema; the transcript may not contain enough evidence.
Delegation fit: the salesperson retains account judgment and all CRM writes.
Simpler alternative: use transcript search and a field checklist.
Value: review burden, recurrence, and current assistance need owner confirmation.
solutions.decision_change: If approved examples require extensive off-call context, narrow the output to evidence retrieval instead of field population.

information_requests.contains: A redacted transcript, the same deal’s MEDDPICC fields before and after the call, and the salesperson’s corrections or explanation, linked by one shared example ID.
information_requests.why: This reveals the actual transformation and what information came from outside the call.
information_requests.decision_change: Decide whether to propose field drafts, evidence retrieval, or no new assistance.
information_requests.acceptable_substitute: Walk through one representative call and the resulting field updates; mark anything reconstructed from memory.

information_requests.artifact: The qualification rubric or working checklist
information_requests.contains: Field definitions, examples of an acceptable update, and when a field should remain unknown.
information_requests.why: A field name alone does not reveal the standard that a useful suggestion must satisfy.
information_requests.decision_change: Determine whether there is a stable, checkable output standard.
information_requests.acceptable_substitute: The sales owner can annotate the linked example with the rule used for each field.

information_requests.contains: An example where a suggestion was misleading or where several conversations were needed, plus the corrected outcome.
information_requests.why: This tests the counter-hypothesis instead of only confirming the happy path.
information_requests.decision_change: Set the scope boundary and determine when the assistant should abstain.
information_requests.acceptable_substitute: Describe a recent failure and the missing context; retain uncertainty until an example is available.

continuation.feedback_request: Does this describe your work, what already helps, and where is the main misunderstanding?

avoid.name: Unreviewed automatic CRM updates
avoid.reason: The illustrative constraints retain salesperson judgment and do not establish permission for writes.

guardrails: No CRM write or implementation is authorized by selecting this recommendation.
Keep account judgment with the salesperson.

evidence.scope_notes: All examples are synthetic. The record preserves two process memberships and a proposed bridge for testing portable export, without claiming a production workflow.
